LESSON: FRACTIONS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.6: FRACTIONS
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers FRACTIONS, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How do you use fractions in real life? 2. How can you represent fractions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on FRACTIONS together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Encourage others to keep trying too when learners work in pairs/groups writing fractions to

represent as part of a whole or part of a group.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: use any available material to research and present on how to convert

improper fractions to mixed fractions.

Values:
● Responsibility: learners represent fractions as part of a whole and as part of a group using concrete objects such as

counters and takes care of the objects and other learning materials.

● Respect: learners in groups discuss and appreciate diverse opinions on the top (numerator) and bottom

(denominator) numbers in a fraction and share with other groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Peer education and mentorship: as learners help each other to convert improper fractions to mixed fractions.

● Safety and security: as learners use sharp objects to make paper cut outs to represent proper, improper and mixed

fractions as part of a whole or as part of a group.

27

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate fractions as part of a whole or part of a group using cut outs, counters or clock face to

mixtures in Science and Technology

Suggested Learning Resources:

Equivalent fraction board, Circular and rectangular cut outs, counters, relevant digital devices, realia
